sections.en: 2-3 μὲν κατ’ ἀποτομὴν οὐ ῥᾷον ('on the one hand by cutting off not easier') A. 3 δεσπότου ('of the master') Mai. 4 τῶν ἀστέρων ('of the stars'), in the margin written τοῦ Ἄρεως ('of Mars') A. τετραγώνων ('of squares') Mai. 5 μὲν ('on the one hand') omitted by A. 6 ἵνα ('in order that') A : ἃ ('which things') Mai. 8 ἐπιτείνοντο ('they were stretched') Mai . ἐπιγένοιντο ('they might happen') A. 8 τὰ ('the') Mai : τὸ ('the') A. 9 σημαίνοντα ('signifying'), in the margin written συμβαίνοντα ('happening') A. 10 ἡμῶν ('of us') omitted by A. πρότερον ('formerly') and νῦν ('now') written above the line by A. 10-11 πρὸς τὴν ἑκάστην καταρχὴν ('towards each inception') but in the margin just as Mai, A. 11 ἀπὸ τῆς ('from the') written above the line by A. 12 αὐτῆς ('of her/it') written above the line by A. 12-13 διηγγέλθησαν οἱ πολέμιοι ('the enemies were announced') (οἱ πολ. ['the en.'] written above the line). After διηγγέλθησαν ('were announced') something seems to be missing. 13-14 ἢ εἰσβεβλ. - εἰρημένων ('or having invaded - of the things said') omitted by A, who has these things: καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦδε πῶς πρ. ἐπ. ἀμφότερον σκοπεῖν προσέσθαι εἴτε κρατοῦσιν οἱ ἐπιόντες εἴτε καὶ μή ('and from this how ... both to consider to add whether the attackers prevail or even not'). 15 κρατεῖεν ('they might prevail') Mai. 16 ἐκείνων ('of those') the codices have; corrected by Kroll. 16-17 δεῖ - μέλλοντος] ('it is necessary - of the future]') ἡ κρίσις ('the judgment') the rest omitted by A. 17 διαγινώσκει ('distinguishes') A. 18 καὶ βεβαία ('and firm') omitted by A. ἔσται - ἡ πρόγνωσις ('will be - the foreknowledge') written above the line; in the text: ἡ ἀπόφασις ('the declaration') A. 19-20 αὐτοὺς ἢ τοὺς κακοποιοὺς ἢ τετραγώνους, εἰ κατάρχουσιν ἐτῶν ἢ ('them or the malefics or squares, if they rule the years or') conjectured by Boll. Concerning ἐπεμβάσει ('intervention') compare Kroll, Gött. Gel. Anzeig., 1900, p. 971. 20 ἐτῶν καὶ ('of years and') Mai : ἐκ τῶν ('out of the') A.

sections.en: 1 The chapter of Dorotheus "De absentis reditu" ("On the return of the absent") translated from the Arabic language into Latin is found in the Book of Nine Judges in the Judgments of the stars published by Petrus Liechtenstein at Venice in the year 1508, f. 74v (= p. 546, edition of the year 1571).

summary.headline: Astrology of War and Illness
summary.text: Chapter 63, “On the resolution of war,” explains judging the outcome and duration of conflict from the lower midheaven, Mars places, squares, benefics, malefics, sect, solid signs, lunar transits, and the nativities of the attackers, attacked city, and leader, with reference to Dorotheus. The page then begins Hermes’ method for diagnosing recovery from illness by calculating the patient’s name, treatment day, seven vowels, and lunar day, and dividing the total by three.
